report_name: AI Weaponized in Supply Chain Attacks on Uber, Ceva, and Fairlife

threat_actors.name: Unattributed AI-powered Supply Chain Attackers
threat_actors.description: A general threat actor persona representing the entities described in the article who are weaponizing AI to conduct supply chain attacks against logistics and manufacturing companies like Uber Freight, Ceva Logistics, and Fairlife.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Attackers targeted the supply chains of major companies, compromising suppliers or partners to gain access to the primary targets' networks.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: A ransomware attack was used against Fairlife, forcing a temporary shutdown of its U.S. operations by encrypting data.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Adversaries exploited trusted relationships between companies and their suppliers or partners to facilitate initial access into logistics networks.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use AI-powered reconnaissance to scan for vulnerabilities across a target's network of suppliers and partners, identifying weak links for exploitation much faster than manual methods.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: AI is used to generate highly convincing and personalized phishing emails at scale to target key personnel in logistics firms for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Impair Defenses
attack_patterns.description: AI-driven malware was described as being able to learn and adapt to a target's security environment, modifying its behavior to evade detection by traditional signature-based security tools.

tools.name: Artificial Intelligence
tools.description: Used as a dual-use technology by attackers to automate reconnaissance, generate sophisticated social engineering content, and create malware that evades traditional defenses.

identities.name: Uber Freight
identities.description: A division of Uber that experienced a security incident involving unauthorized system access as part of a wave of supply chain attacks.

identities.name: Ceva Logistics
identities.description: A subsidiary of CMA CGM that reported a data breach leaking customer information.

identities.name: Fairlife
identities.description: A dairy brand owned by The Coca-Cola Company that was hit by a ransomware attack, forcing a temporary shutdown of its U.S. operations.

identities.name: Jaguar Land Rover
identities.description: Cited as a previous victim of a supply chain attack that caused a major production halt.

identities.name: The Coca-Cola Company
identities.description: The parent company of Fairlife, which was impacted by a ransomware attack.

indicators.name: Potential DGA DNS Queries
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential DGA DNS Queries
id: 2b1c8e9f-4d5a-4b6c-8e7f-9a8b7c6d5e4f
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS queries with high entropy, which can be indicative of Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) used by AI-driven malware as mentioned in hunting hints for supply chain attacks.
references:
  - https://www.businessinsider.com/supply-chain-cyberattacks-ai-to-fight-ai-2026-9
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-12
tags:
  - attack.t1568.002
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|re: '(?i)^[a-z0-9]{20,}\.(com|net|org|biz|info)$'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries with high entropy, which can be indicative of Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) used by AI-driven malware as mentioned in hunting hints for supply chain attacks.

indicators.name: Anomalous API Access from Partner Connections
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous API Access from Partner Connections
id: 8c7d6e5f-4b3a-4c2d-8e1f-9a8b7c6d5e4d
status: experimental
description: Detects a high volume of client or server errors from a single partner IP address accessing an API, which could indicate a compromised supplier attempting to exploit an API endpoint.
references:
  - https://www.businessinsider.com/supply-chain-cyberattacks-ai-to-fight-ai-2026-9
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-12
tags:
  - attack.t1195
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    sc_status|startswith: 
      - '4'
      - '5'
  condition: selection | count(c_uri) by c_ip > 20
indicators.description: Detects a high volume of client or server errors from a single partner IP address accessing an API, which could indicate a compromised supplier attempting to exploit an API endpoint, as suggested by hunting hints.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous API Access from Partner Connections
